cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Give It Up
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender something they value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Would you sell your signed guitar so we can replace the fridge?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I queued all night for that signature.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then let's price it properly. Those hours should buy us an ice maker.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll sell the case. The guitar stays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the case. You can still tell the queue story while I photograph the guitar.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 queue effort causes A3 pricing argument; A3 question delay is unrelated, while B4 case-only offer is used by A5.

relationship.evidence: B2 explains sentimental investment and B4 offers a limited sacrifice, giving A persuasion a credible obstacle.

heightening.evidence: B4 protects the guitar by offering its case; A5 reverses which item stays while preserving the story.
